title: Unit-normalized reflection of coefficient squares and their adjunction mates
statement:
For $i=0,1$ let $\mathcal A_i,\mathcal B_i$ be categories, each with a full reflective subcategory of local objects. Write $\Lambda_{i,T}$ for the reflector followed by inclusion and $\eta_{i,T}:\operatorname{id}\to\Lambda_{i,T}$ for its unit, with $T=A,B$. Thus $\Lambda_{i,T}M$ is local and precomposition with $\eta_M$ bijects maps to every local object. Let $F_i:\mathcal A_i\rightleftarrows\mathcal B_i:G_i$ be specified adjunctions [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. Assume $G_i$ sends local objects to local objects and is equipped with a natural isomorphism $\gamma_i:\Lambda_{i,A}G_i\xrightarrow{\sim}G_i\Lambda_{i,B}$ satisfying $\gamma_{i,M}\eta_{i,A,G_iM}=G_i(\eta_{i,B,M})$.

Let $C_A:\mathcal A_0\to\mathcal A_1$, $C_B:\mathcal B_0\to\mathcal B_1$ have natural isomorphisms $\kappa_T:C_T\Lambda_{0,T}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_{1,T}C_T$ satisfying $\kappa_{T,M}C_T(\eta_{0,T,M})=\eta_{1,T,C_TM}$. Let $\delta:F_1C_A\xrightarrow{\sim}C_BF_0$, and let $\beta:C_AG_0\to G_1C_B$ be its right mate for the specified adjunctions.

Then $\widehat F_i=\Lambda_{i,B}F_i$ on local inputs is left adjoint to the restriction $\widehat G_i$ of $G_i$, with Hom bijection obtained by precomposing with the reflection unit and then taking the original adjunct. The $C_T$ preserve local objects. On local inputs the induced comparison
$$\widehat\delta=\kappa_B^{-1}\circ\Lambda_{1,B}(\delta):\widehat F_1C_A\xrightarrow{\sim}C_B\widehat F_0$$
has right mate precisely the restriction of $\beta$. On every ambient $M\in\mathcal B_0$ one has the normalization equation
$$\beta_{\Lambda_{0,B}M}\,C_A(\gamma_{0,M})=G_1(\kappa_{B,M}^{-1})\,\gamma_{1,C_BM}\,\Lambda_{1,A}(\beta_M)\,\kappa_{A,G_0M}.$$
For composable diagrams with these data, pasting coefficient squares or pasting adjunctions before this construction gives the same comparisons as pasting afterwards, using the composition comparisons determined by the displayed Hom bijections. Identity squares give the identity comparisons. If the categories have shifts and all the specified functors, units, $\gamma$, $\kappa$ and $\delta$ respect them, these conclusions respect shifts as well. No invertibility of $\beta$ is assumed.

proof.text: Use right-to-left composition throughout, and distinguish reflection units $\eta$ from adjunction units $u_i$ and counits $e_i$. An object $X$ is local exactly when $\eta_X$ is invertible: if $X$ is local, the reflection bijection supplies $r:\Lambda X\to X$ with $r\eta_X=1_X$, and its injectivity into the local object $\Lambda X$ gives $\eta_Xr=1_{\Lambda X}$; conversely an invertible $\eta_X$ identifies $X$ with the local object $\Lambda X$. Here local objects mean the isomorphism-closed essential image of the full reflective inclusion. For local $X$, the assumed equation $\eta_{1,T,C_TX}=\kappa_{T,X}C_T(\eta_{0,T,X})$ is a composite of isomorphisms. Thus $C_TX$ is local, for both $T=A,B$. Restrictions of $C_T$ and $G_i$ to the full local subcategories therefore exist.

proof.text:
For local $X\in\mathcal A_i$ and $Y\in\mathcal B_i$, put $k_{i,X}=\eta_{i,B,F_iX}$ and let $H_i$ be the original adjunction bijection. Define $\widehat H_i(t)=H_i(tk_{i,X})$ for $t:\Lambda_{i,B}F_iX\to Y$. This is a bijection because $Y$ is local and precomposition by $k_{i,X}$ is the reflection bijection. For $a:X'\to X$ and $b:Y\to Y'$, naturality of $\eta$ and $H_i$ gives
$$\widehat H_i(b\,t\,\Lambda_{i,B}F_i(a))=G_i(b)\widehat H_i(t)a.$$
Apply the cited natural-Hom-bijection theorem to obtain $\widehat F_i\dashv\widehat G_i$ with this precise bijection. Its unit and counit are consequently
$$\widehat u_{i,X}=G_i(k_{i,X})u_{i,X},\qquad \widehat e_{i,Y}k_{i,G_iY}=e_{i,Y}.$$
The counit equation determines $\widehat e$ uniquely because its target $Y$ is local. No identification of adjunctions other than this specified Hom bijection is made.

proof.text:
The proposed $\widehat\delta_X=\kappa_{B,F_0X}^{-1}\Lambda_{1,B}(\delta_X)$ is a natural isomorphism between local objects when $X$ is local. Naturality of the reflection unit and the normalization of $\kappa_B$ give the crucial equation
$$\widehat\delta_Xk_{1,C_AX}=C_B(k_{0,X})\delta_X.\tag{*}$$
Indeed, $\Lambda_{1,B}(\delta_X)\eta_{1,B,F_1C_AX}=\eta_{1,B,C_BF_0X}\delta_X$, and $\kappa_{B,F_0X}^{-1}\eta_{1,B,C_BF_0X}=C_B(\eta_{0,B,F_0X})$. This also proves uniqueness of $\widehat\delta$ subject to (*) by injectivity of the reflection bijection into the local target $C_B\widehat F_0X$.

proof.text:
Fix local $Y\in\mathcal B_0$. By the mate definition, the reflected mate at $Y$ is the $\widehat F_1\dashv\widehat G_1$ adjunct of
$$t=C_B(\widehat e_{0,Y})\widehat\delta_{G_0Y}:\widehat F_1C_AG_0Y\to C_BY.$$
All inputs are local by step 1 and the hypothesis on $G_0$. Equation (*) and step 2 imply
$$tk_{1,C_AG_0Y}=C_B(\widehat e_{0,Y}k_{0,G_0Y})\delta_{G_0Y}=C_B(e_{0,Y})\delta_{G_0Y}.$$
Its ordinary $F_1\dashv G_1$ adjunct is exactly $\beta_Y$, by the same mate definition. The definition of $\widehat H_1$ in step 2 therefore says that the reflected mate is $\beta_Y$ itself. This uses no invertibility of $\beta$.

proof.text:
For ambient $M\in\mathcal B_0$, both sides of the claimed normalization equation are maps from $C_A\Lambda_{0,A}G_0M$ to the local object $G_1C_B\Lambda_{0,B}M$. Precomposition with $C_A(\eta_{0,A,G_0M})$ is injective: under $\kappa_{A,G_0M}$ it is precomposition with $\eta_{1,A,C_AG_0M}$, whose target-testing bijection applies. After this precomposition, the left side becomes
$$\beta_{\Lambda_{0,B}M}C_AG_0(\eta_{0,B,M})=G_1C_B(\eta_{0,B,M})\beta_M$$
by normalization of $\gamma_0$ and naturality of the mate $\beta$. The right side becomes
$$G_1(\kappa_{B,M}^{-1})\gamma_{1,C_BM}\Lambda_{1,A}(\beta_M)\eta_{1,A,C_AG_0M}
=G_1(\kappa_{B,M}^{-1})\gamma_{1,C_BM}\eta_{1,A,G_1C_BM}\beta_M
=G_1(\kappa_{B,M}^{-1}\eta_{1,B,C_BM})\beta_M
=G_1C_B(\eta_{0,B,M})\beta_M.$$
These equalities use, in order, normalization of $\kappa_A$, naturality of $\eta_{1,A}$, normalization of $\gamma_1$, and normalization of $\kappa_B$. Injectivity proves the displayed equation of the statement.

proof.text:
For a second coefficient square $(D_A,D_B,\delta^D)$ from index $1$ to index $2$, use the composite data
$$\kappa^{DC}_{T,X}=\kappa^D_{T,C_TX}D_T(\kappa^C_{T,X}),\qquad
\delta^{DC}_X=D_B(\delta^C_X)\delta^D_{C_AX}.$$
Substituting the two unit equations verifies $\kappa^{DC}_{T,X}D_TC_T(\eta_{0,T,X})=\eta_{2,T,D_TC_TX}$. Compare the reflection of $\delta^{DC}$ with $D_B(\widehat\delta^C_X)\widehat\delta^D_{C_AX}$. Precomposing either map with $k_{2,D_AC_AX}$ gives
$$D_BC_B(k_{0,X})D_B(\delta^C_X)\delta^D_{C_AX},$$
by applying (*) twice. Their common target is local, so the reflection bijection makes the two maps equal. Clause 1 of the cited mate-pasting node gives the right comparison $(\beta^D C_B)\circ(D_A\beta^C)$ both before and after restriction (step 4). Thus coefficient-square pasting commutes with the construction.

source.place: Tags 0E46/0E47, remarks on base-change pasting; use mate-pasting clause 1 and the explicit unit equation

proof.text:
For pasting adjunctions, write a second pair as $H_i:\mathcal B_i\rightleftarrows\mathcal D_i:J_i$, with reflectors $\Lambda_{i,D}$, unit $\eta_{i,D}$, and $J_i$ preserving local objects. For local $X$ set
$$Q_i=\Lambda_{i,D}H_iF_iX,\quad P_i=\Lambda_{i,D}H_i\Lambda_{i,B}F_iX,\quad
q_{i,X}=\Lambda_{i,D}H_i(k_{i,X}):Q_i\to P_i.$$
For local $Z\in\mathcal D_i$, the reflection and $H_i\dashv J_i$ bijections identify precomposition by $q_{i,X}$ with precomposition by $k_{i,X}$ from $\operatorname{Hom}(\Lambda_{i,B}F_iX,J_iZ)$ to $\operatorname{Hom}(F_iX,J_iZ)$. This is bijective since $J_iZ$ is local. Taking $Z=Q_i$ gives $r:P_i\to Q_i$ with $rq_i=1$; injectivity for $Z=P_i$ then gives $q_ir=1$ by precomposing with $q_i$. Thus $q_i$ is a natural isomorphism. Under it the two specified Hom bijections both send a map to its successive $H_i$- and $F_i$-adjunct, after the two reflection units. Hence $q_i$ is precisely the composition comparison specified in the statement, by the composite-Hom-bijection definition of composite adjunction.

source.place: Tag 0DV0, lemma-compose-counits; direct comparison of the two composite Hom bijections

proof.text:
Retain step 7 and add $C_D$ with normalized $\kappa_D$ and a square $\epsilon:H_1C_B\xrightarrow{\sim}C_DH_0$. Write $l_{i,V}=\eta_{i,D,H_iV}$ and $s_{i,X}=\eta_{i,D,H_iF_iX}$, so that
$$q_{i,X}s_{i,X}=l_{i,\widehat F_iX}H_i(k_{i,X}).$$
The ambient pasted square is $\rho_X=\epsilon_{F_0X}H_1(\delta_X)$. The reflected composite on the other route is
$$P_X=\widehat\epsilon_{\widehat F_0X}\widehat H_1(\widehat\delta_X)q_{1,C_AX},$$
where $\widehat H_i=\Lambda_{i,D}H_i$ here denotes the completed second left functor. Using naturality of $l$, equation (*) for both squares, and naturality of $\epsilon$ at $k_{0,X}$ gives
$$P_Xs_{1,C_AX}=C_D(l_{0,\widehat F_0X})\epsilon_{\widehat F_0X}H_1(C_B(k_{0,X})\delta_X)
=C_D(l_{0,\widehat F_0X}H_0(k_{0,X}))\epsilon_{F_0X}H_1(\delta_X)
=C_D(q_{0,X})\widehat\rho_Xs_{1,C_AX}.$$
The target is local, so cancellation by the reflection bijection gives $P_X=C_D(q_{0,X})\widehat\rho_X$. This proves left-square compatibility for adjunction pasting without assuming that $H_i$ preserves local objects. On right adjoints, restriction of $G_iJ_i$ is the composite of their restrictions. Clause 2 of the mate-pasting node now gives exactly the same right square along both routes, since step 7 identifies the adjunctions by their Hom bijections.

source.place: Tags 0E46/0E47, remarks on pasting; mate-pasting clause 2 with the explicit reflector comparison

proof.text:
The composite right adjoint in step 7 also has normalized completion comparison
$$\gamma^{GJ}_M=G(\gamma^J_M)\gamma^G_{JM}.$$
Its composite with $\eta_{A,GJM}$ is $G(\gamma^J_M\eta_{B,JM})=GJ(\eta_{D,M})$, as required. Repeated coefficient pasting has $\kappa$ equal to the iterated product from step 6; its parenthesizations agree by functoriality and associativity. Repeated adjunction pasting has the iterated Hom bijection of the composite-adjunction definition; its parenthesizations agree as compositions of functions. The reflection comparisons are therefore identical by the uniqueness tests in steps 3 and 7, and the mates agree by mate-pasting. With identity coefficient data, (*) becomes $\widehat\delta_Xk_{i,X}=k_{i,X}$ and forces $\widehat\delta=1$; clause 4 of mate-pasting forces its mate to be $1$. The identity adjunction and its reflection on local objects give the identity comparison under $\eta_X^{-1}:\Lambda X\to X$. Thus the identity and iterated-pasting assertions have the required normalization.

source.place: Tags 0037 and 0DV0, units and composite Hom bijections; mate-pasting identity clause

proof.text: Finally assume the given shift compatibilities. The local subcategories are stable under shifts: for local $X$, the shift comparison identifies $\Lambda(X[a])$ with $(\Lambda X)[a]$ and identifies $\eta_{X[a]}$ with the invertible $\eta_X[a]$. The closure rules for shift-compatible transformations show that $\widehat u=G(k)u$, $\widehat\delta=\kappa_B^{-1}\Lambda_B\delta$, and $q=\Lambda_DH(k)$ commute with shifts. Inversion causes no problem: multiplying the commutative shift square for an isomorphism on both sides by its inverse gives the shift square for the inverse. The cited adjunction-shift theorem, clause (i), then gives shift compatibility of the reflected counits from that of their units; it also gives this for the original counits if only unit compatibility was specified. The mate formula from the mate-definition node is a composite of these units, counits and whiskered squares, so the closure rules give shift compatibility of $\beta$ and its reflected restriction. Every product in the normalization and pasting equations is consequently shift-compatible. This proves the final assertion for all specified shifts.
